newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Yusen shares fall after tanker oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Yusen shares fall after tanker oil spill.

text.p: Shares of leading shipping company Nippon Yusen KK fell on Wednesday afternoon in Tokyo after a supertanker owned by the company scraped a reef in shallow waters of Tokyo Bay and spilled crude oil.
By 0551 GMT, Nippon Yusen shares were down six yen at 434.
Japan's coastguard said an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil may have leaked from the 259,999 deadweight-tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace, making it one of Japan's biggest ever oil spills.
The very large crude carrier (VLCC) had been on its way to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's 75,000 barrel-per-day refinery in Kawasaki, near Tokyo, a Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said.
Mitsubishi Oil shares closed at 512 yen, up 10 yen from its Tuesday's close.
